hook: ChatGPT keeps explaining things to me like I'm a curious 12-year-old. I have a PhD.
caption:
ChatGPT keeps explaining things to me like I'm a curious 12-year-old. I have a PhD.

Not a complaint about AI. A complaint about AI that doesn't know who it's talking to.

Here's what actually happens:

You ask a complex question about, say, monetary policy transmission mechanisms.

And it starts with: "Great question! Money is something we use to buy things..."

You die a little inside.

The model isn't dumb. It's just calibrated for the average person asking that question — not YOU.

The fix isn't prompting harder every single time. The fix is a profile that tells the AI, once, permanently:

→ Your actual expertise level
→ How you like information structured
→ Whether you want the nuance or just the conclusion
→ What kind of examples actually land for you

When the AI knows you think in frameworks, it skips the kindergarten intro.
When it knows you want the contrarian take, it stops giving you the Wikipedia version.
When it knows you're an expert, it treats you like one.

You shouldn't have to earn that every conversation.

That's what bootfile.ai is for. One profile. Every conversation, finally calibrated.

Link in bio — takes 5 minutes to build yours.
